chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is not befitting for the free man that he marries the slave girl while he is able to marry the free woman, and it is not befitting that he marries the slave girl in addition to the free woman; and there is no problem if he marries the free woman in addition to the slave girl. So if he were to marry the free woman in addition to the slave girl, then for the free woman is two days, and for the slave girl is one day.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a free man marrying a slave girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the juristic preference (istihbab) for a free man to prioritize marrying a free woman, though marrying a slave girl is permissible if he cannot afford a free wife. It further clarifies the practical application of polygyny by mandating an equal distribution of conjugal time, granting the free wife two days for every one day allotted to the slave wife, reflecting the social hierarchy within the household. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the rights and status of concubines versus wives in classical Islamic society.
